Class VanillaScreenPanelAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.inject.VanillaScreenPanelAdapter
public final class VanillaScreenPanelAdapter extends Object
Phase 18s — sibling to ScreenPanelAdapter that anchors MK panels onto vanilla NON-container screens — the Options screen, Controls, KeyBinds, world-select, server-list, anywhere Screen is the superclass rather than AbstractContainerScreen.

Why a sibling, not an extension

ScreenPanelAdapter is built around the inventory-chrome model — MenuRegion anchors against leftPos/topPos/ imageWidth/imageHeight; MenuChrome extends those bounds by the screen's chrome extents; its origin resolution takes an AbstractContainerScreen<?>. None of that applies to non-container screens (which have no inventory chrome — they fill the whole screen). Trying to unify the two would bifurcate the API per call site; sibling-with-its-own-vocabulary keeps each call site type-correct.

Same registry, separate dispatch path

ScreenPanelRegistry's AFTER_INIT listener already fires for every opened screen — the container-screen filter happens at the dispatch layer. Phase 18s extends that listener to branch on screen type: container screens still go through ScreenPanelRegistry's existing logic; non-container screens route to VanillaScreenPanelRegistry for the parallel dispatch path (render via addRenderableOnly, input via Fabric's ScreenMouseEvents).

Lifecycle parallels ScreenPanelAdapter

  1. Construct with a Panel, a ScreenRegion, and a padding (and optionally a RegionAnchor for explicit priority). Constructor registers the panel with the RegionRegistry and tracks the adapter in VanillaScreenPanelRegistry's pending set.
  2. Call .on(Class...) or .onAny() to declare targeting. Targeting moves the adapter from pending to registered. Targeting must be declared exactly once.
  3. When a matching screen opens, the registry dispatches render + input to the adapter.

Input contract

MK panels EAT clicks within their bounds — vanilla widgets behind the panel are NOT dispatched to when the click lands inside the panel. Mirrors the default Panel.opaque(true) contract of the container-screen path. Clicks outside the panel bounds fall through to vanilla's widget dispatch unchanged.

v1 scope

Region-based only (no lambda-origin escape hatch — consumers who need bespoke positioning on a vanilla screen can either write their own Screen mixin or use the ScreenRegion anchors). No modal / dim-behind / hover-suppression machinery (no consumer has surfaced the need for modals on vanilla screens yet). Fold-on-evidence for both.

  • Constructor Details

    • VanillaScreenPanelAdapter

      public VanillaScreenPanelAdapter(Panel panel, ScreenRegion region, int padding)
      Region-aware constructor with explicit padding. Registers the panel into the given ScreenRegion via RegionRegistry with the declared padding so stacking math and overflow checks both account for it. Uses RegionAnchor.DEFAULT_PRIORITY for sibling ordering.

    • VanillaScreenPanelAdapter

      public VanillaScreenPanelAdapter(Panel panel, RegionAnchor<ScreenRegion> anchor)
      Region-aware constructor accepting a RegionAnchor — region paired with an explicit stacking priority. Padding defers to Panel.interiorPadding() (0 for NONE, 7 otherwise — same style-conditional default as ScreenPanelAdapter).

    • VanillaScreenPanelAdapter

      public VanillaScreenPanelAdapter(Panel panel, RegionAnchor<ScreenRegion> anchor, int padding)
      Region-aware constructor with both explicit padding and priority.

  • Method Details

    • on

      @SafeVarargs public final VanillaScreenPanelAdapter on(Class<? extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen>... screenClasses)
      Declares the screen classes this adapter applies to. Resolution is class-ancestry — the adapter fires on any opened Screen that is an instance of one or more of screenClasses.

      Multi-target semantics are OR — any matching target fires the adapter. Call exactly once. Duplicate declarations throw.

    • onAny

      public VanillaScreenPanelAdapter onAny()
      Declares this adapter fires on every opened non-container Screen. Rare for vanilla screens (the panel would appear on every menu screen the user navigates — title, options, world-select, etc.); typically consumers want a specific class. .on(Class...) is preferred.

    • unregister

      public void unregister()
      Removes this adapter from every internal registry collection. Idempotent. After unregister() the adapter contributes nothing to layout, dispatch, or rendering.

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(int sw, int sh, double mouseX, double mouseY, int button, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Dispatches a mouse click to any visible element under the cursor. Returns true if any element consumed the click — OR if the click landed inside the panel's outer bounds but no element claimed it (eats the click per the input-contract — panels are opaque to vanilla-widget dispatch within their bounds).

      Pass ordering matters. The active-overlay pass runs FIRST, unconditionally — overlay extents (PanelElement.getActiveOverlayBounds()) can reach OUTSIDE the panel's outer layout bounds (Dropdown popovers, etc.), so gating the overlay loop on an inPanel check would swallow popover clicks. Bug surfaced by Imp@Keybindery on 2026-05-19 (controls-screen Sort/Filter dropdowns lost their selection clicks); fix landed in menukit/(this commit).

    • notifyOutsideClick

      public void notifyOutsideClick(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Notifies this adapter's visible elements of an outside click so popover- like elements (Dropdown/DropdownMulti) can dismiss. Each element self-guards via PanelElement.notifyClickOutsideOverlay(double, double) (it closes only if the click fell outside its own overlay/trigger), so the registry can call this on every adapter for every click regardless of which adapter consumed it. The vanilla-screen twin of MKScreen's dismiss janitor. Coordinates are screen-space (elements cache their own screen positions at render, so no origin is needed here).

    • mouseReleased

      public boolean mouseReleased(double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Dispatches a mouse-release event to all visible elements. NOT hit-tested (release fires for every visible element so drag-end detection works when the cursor has moved off during drag).

    • keyPressed

      public boolean keyPressed(int keyCode, int scanCode, int modifiers)
      Dispatches a key press to this adapter's visible elements (keyboard-nav completion — keyboard parallel to mouseClicked(int, int, double, double, int, Screen)). NOT hit-tested; every visible element is offered the key until one consumes it. Returns true once consumed so the caller eats the key from vanilla. Canonical consumer: an open Dropdown.
